name: expo-app

scripts.bundle:verify: bun run check:versions && bun run bundle:ios && bun run bundle:hermes && bun run check:launch-path

//: BUILD SAFETY — `overrides`/`resolutions` exist because declaring a version
in `dependencies` was not enough to get that version into a build.
`expo-web-browser` was corrected to `~15.0.11` and the very next Android
build (versionCode 14) still shipped the 56.x native module: it died on
open with `NoClassDefFoundError: expo.modules.kotlin.types.AnyTypeCache` at
`WebBrowserModule.definition`, a class that only exists in the SDK 56+
expo-modules-core. The dependency block said one thing and the installer
resolved another.
The mechanism is `@rork-ai/toolkit-sdk`, which peer-depends on
`expo-web-browser: "*"` (also `expo-blur: "*"` and `expo-router: "*"`).
`*` matches every version ever published, so an installer that satisfies
that peer on its own terms — npm 7+ auto-installs peers — is free to fetch
the newest release and hoist it over ours. That is almost certainly how the
`^56.0.5` caret arrived in this file in the first place.
`overrides` (npm/pnpm) and `resolutions` (yarn/bun) are the two spellings of
'no resolver may choose anything else'. Both are listed because this repo is
installed by bun locally and in CI, and by Rork's builder in the cloud, and
the build that reaches a store is the one that matters.
Keep every version here EXACT and identical to the `dependencies` entry.
`bun run check:versions` fails the build if they drift apart or off the SDK.
